```{r setup}
library(panelcointr)
```

## The tests

Banerjee and Carrion-i-Silvestre (2015) test the null hypothesis of no
cointegration in panels whose units share unobserved common factors and may
have structural breaks. For unit $i$,

$$
y_{it} = D_{it} + x_{it}' \delta_{it} + u_{it}, \qquad
u_{it} = F_t' \pi_i + e_{it},
$$

where $D_{it}$ holds a constant, possibly a trend, and level and trend
shifts, and $\delta_{it}$ may shift at the break dates. The factors $F_t$
may be I(0) or I(1). The test follows the PANIC approach of Bai and Ng
(2004): each unit's cointegrating regression is estimated in first
differences, the common factors are extracted from the residuals by
principal components, and the defactored residuals are cumulated and tested
for a unit root with ADF regressions. The pooled statistic

$$
Z = \sqrt{N}\, \frac{\bar t - \Theta}{\sqrt{\Psi}}
$$

is asymptotically standard normal and left-tailed. Rejecting means that the
idiosyncratic errors are stationary; the variables are cointegrated only if,
in addition, no common factor is I(1). The factors are therefore tested
separately: by an ADF test when there is one, and by the MQ tests of Bai and
Ng (2004) when there are several.

## A simulated panel

We simulate 30 units over 80 years with one I(1) common factor, a regressor
whose coefficient shifts in 1990, and cointegrated idiosyncratic errors.

```{r data}
set.seed(42)
N <- 30
T <- 80
years <- 1950 + seq_len(T)
f <- cumsum(rnorm(T))
d <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(N), function(i) {
  x <- cumsum(rnorm(T))
  e <- as.numeric(stats::filter(rnorm(T), 0.5, method = "recursive"))
  y <- 1 + 0.02 * seq_len(T) + x + 0.5 * (years > 1990) * x + rnorm(1, 1) * f + e
  data.frame(country = i, year = years, y = y, x = x)
}))
```

## Known breaks

The break date is the last year of the old regime. Model 5 has a constant, a
trend, a level shift and a shift in the cointegrating vector:

```{r known}
fit <- pcoint_banerjee(y ~ x, data = d, index = c("country", "year"),
                       model = 5, breaks = 1990)
fit
```

The idiosyncratic errors are stationary (Z rejects), but the common factor
is I(1): `y` and `x` cointegrate only together with the common stochastic
trend. `summary()` adds the unit-level ADF tests, the factor-number
criterion and the selected lags:

```{r summary}
summary(fit)
```

## Estimated breaks

With `breaks = 1` or `2`, the dates are estimated. Heterogeneous dates
(one per unit) come from an iterative least-squares procedure that
alternates between the break dates and the common factors:

```{r hetero}
het <- pcoint_banerjee(y ~ x, data = d, index = c("country", "year"),
                       model = 5, breaks = 1)
table(het$units$break_date)
het$statistics
```

Common dates are chosen to minimise the statistic; the paper's Table III
gives finite-sample critical values for this infimum. `plot()` shows the
profile over the candidate dates:

```{r homog, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 4}
hom <- pcoint_banerjee(y ~ x, data = d, index = c("country", "year"),
                       model = 2, breaks = 1, break_type = "homogeneous")
hom$statistics
plot(hom)
```

In simulations of the paper's own design, the infimum statistic in Model 5
over-rejects when the cointegrating vector shifts a lot (see
`inst/validation/RESULTS.md`); known dates or heterogeneous estimation are
safer there.

## Settings

`factors` fixes the number of factors or chooses the criterion (BIC3 of Bai
and Ng 2002 by default, at most `max_factors = 6`), `lags` the ADF lag order
(t-sig rule of Ng and Perron 1995 by default) and `dols` adds leads and lags
of $\Delta^2 x$ for endogenous regressors. `banerjee_control()` holds the
rest: the lag rule, the standardisation of the residuals before the
principal components, finite-sample moments, and the MQ settings.

## References

Bai, J. and Ng, S. (2002). Determining the number of factors in approximate
factor models. *Econometrica* 70(1), 191-221.

Bai, J. and Ng, S. (2004). A PANIC attack on unit roots and cointegration.
*Econometrica* 72(4), 1127-1177.

Banerjee, A. and Carrion-i-Silvestre, J. L. (2015). Cointegration in panel
data with structural breaks and cross-section dependence. *Journal of
Applied Econometrics* 30(1), 1-23.

Ng, S. and Perron, P. (1995). Unit root tests in ARMA models with
data-dependent methods for the selection of the truncation lag. *Journal of
the American Statistical Association* 90, 268-281.
